Rashi on Nazir 15b:10:1.hebrew: ואף רבי אושעיא סבר - דרבי יוסי לא אמר דמטמא למפרע אלא מדרבנן. ומהדר אהא דאמר לעיל: ״מאי למפרע — מדרבנן״:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:10:1.english: And even Rabbi Oshaya holds - That Rabbi Yosei said that he renders [objects] impure retroactively only by rabbinic law. And [the Gemara] returns to that which it said above: “What is [the meaning of] retroactively? By rabbinic law.”

Rashi on Nazir 15b:11:1.hebrew: אי סתר - דלמפרע טמאה, כולהו לסתור, דהא לא הוו להו שבעה נקיים כלל:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:11:1.english: If it negates - That [if] retroactively she is impure, it should negate all of them, for there were not seven clean [days] at all.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:11:2.hebrew: אלא אימא ולא לסתור אפילו יומו - משום דמכאן ולהבא מטמאה, ולמפרע הויא טהורה ממש:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:11:2.english: Rather, say: And it should not negate even its [own] day - Because from here on she becomes impure, and retroactively she was genuinely pure.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:1:1.hebrew: אבא שאול אומר כו' מצות אבילות הנוהגת שלשה ימים הראשונים - כיון שעשאם קודם הרגל, בטל הימנו גזירת ז' לגמרי. כך מצות ז', כיון שנעשו קודם הרגל, שוב הרגל מבטל גזירת ל' לגמרי. גזירת ל' — גלוח וכיבוס:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:1:1.english: Abba Shaul says, etc.: The mitzva of mourning that is practiced [during] the first three days - Since he observed them before the Festival, the decree of seven [days] was completely nullified for him. So too, [regarding] the mitzva of seven [days]: since they were observed before the Festival, the Festival then completely nullifies the decree of thirty [days]. The decree of thirty [consists of the prohibition against] haircutting and laundering.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:2:1.hebrew: מ"ט דאבא שאול - דאמר דיום ז' מבטלת גזירת ז' ול', והא לא שימר עדיין מיום ל' כלום קודם הרגל, אפי' יום אחד! דבשלמא לת"ק דאמר שמנה, היינו משום דיום שמיני עולה למנין ל'. אלא לאבא שאול, מ"ט? לאו משום דקסבר דיום שביעי עולה לכאן ולכאן — למנין ז' ולמנין ל' — וכמאן דעבר עליו יום אחד מגזירת ל' דמי, ומש"ה מתבטלת:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:2:1.english: What is the rationale of Abba Shaul - For he said that [observing] the seventh day cancels the decree of seven and thirty [days of mourning], and yet he has not yet observed anything of the thirty [days] prior to the Festival, not even a single day! For it is well according to the first tanna, who said eight [days], that is because the eighth day counts toward the tally of thirty. But according to Abba Shaul, what is the rationale? Is it not because he holds that the seventh day counts for here and there — for the tally of seven and for the tally of thirty — and he is considered like one for whom one day of the decree of thirty has passed, and for that reason [the decree of thirty] is voided?

Rashi on Nazir 15b:2:2.hebrew: אלא באבילות דרבנן - דעיקר אבילות אינו אלא יום אחד, דכתיב (עמוס ח) ואחריתה כיום מר, אלא רבנן תקנו ז', דסמכו אקרא, כדכתיב (בראשית נ) ויעש לאביו אבל שבעת ימים; אבל נזירות דאורייתא, בחושבנא דיומי — דל' יום בעינן, כדכתיב (במדבר ו) יהיה — לא אמר דיום אחד עולה לכאן ולכאן:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:2:2.english: Only with regard to mourning, which is rabbinic - For the primary [obligation of] mourning is only one day, as it is written: “And the end thereof as a bitter day” (Amos 8:10); rather, the Rabbis instituted seven [days], as they relied upon a verse, as it is written: “And he made a mourning for his father seven days” (Genesis 50:10). But [regarding] naziriteship, which is by Torah law, in the tally of days — for we require thirty days, as it is written: “[Holy] shall he be” (Numbers 6:5) [where the numerical value of yihyeh is thirty] — he did not say that one day counts for here and there.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:3:1.hebrew: ששחטו וזרקו עליה בשני שלה - שכבר ראתה ביום שמיני, עד שלא ראתה ביום תשיעי, שהיא שומרת כנגדו, לידע אם תראה בג' ימים ג' ראיות ותהא זבה:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:3:1.english: That they slaughtered and sprinkled for her on her second [day] - For she had already experienced a discharge on the eighth day, before she experienced a discharge on the ninth day, which she observes corresponding to it, to know whether she will experience three discharges in three days and become a zavah.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:4:1.hebrew: ואח"כ ראתה הרי זו אינה אוכלת - בפסח, דטמאה היא. ואע"ג דאינה אוכלת, פטורה מלעשות פסח שני, דאכילת פסחים לא מיעכבא:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:4:1.english: And after that she saw, behold, she may not eat - From the Paschal offering, for she is ritually impure. And even though she does not eat, she is exempt from observing the second Pesach, for the eating of Paschal offerings is not indispensable.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:5:1.hebrew: מ"ט דר' יוסי - דפטורה מלעשות פסח שני, לאו משום דקסבר מקצת היום ככולו, דיום שני — שהוא תשיעי — ככולו דמי, והויא לה טהורה בשעה ששחטו וזרקו עליה? והכא נמי, לימא דעולה לו לכאן ולכאן משום דמקצת היום ככולו:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:5:1.english: What is the rationale of Rabbi Yosei - [in ruling] that she is exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ: Is it not because he holds [that] part of the day is like the whole of it, [such] that the second day — which is the ninth — is considered like all of it, and she was ritually pure at the time when they slaughtered and sprinkled [the blood] on her behalf? And here too, let us say that [the day] counts for him in both directions because part of the day is like the whole of it.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:5:2.hebrew: דילמא - האי דקאמר ר' יוסי דפטורה, לאו משום דקסבר דמקצת היום ככולו, אלא משום דקסבר דכשהיא רואה, מכאן ולהבא היא מטמאה, אבל למפרע לא. ומשום הכי פטורה — דבההיא שעתא דשחטו וזרקו עליה טהורה הואי, ולהך דבתר נטמאת לא חיישינן:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:5:2.english: Perhaps - That which Rabbi Yosei said, that she is exempt, is not because he holds that part of the day is like the whole of it, but rather because he holds that when she experiences a discharge, she becomes impure from now and onward, but not retroactively. And on account of this she is exempt, for at that time when they slaughtered [the Paschal offering] and sprinkled [the blood] on her behalf, she was pure, and as for that which she became impure afterward, we do not take [it] into account.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:6:1.hebrew: ומי סבר ר' יוסי - דמכאן ולהבא היא מטמאה, אבל למפרע לא:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:6:1.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold - That from now onward she becomes impure, but retroactively [she does] not?

Rashi on Nazir 15b:7:1.hebrew: זב בעל שתי ראיות - בין ביום אחד, בין בשני ימים, כדאמרי' התם (ב"ק דף כד.): תלה הכתוב את הזב בראיות, דכתיב: "וזאת תהיה טומאתו בזובו", ואת הזבה בימים, דכתיב: "ואשה כי יזוב זוב דמה ימים רבים" — מיעוט ימים — שנים, רבים — ג':
Rashi on Nazir 15b:7:1.english: A zav who has had two sightings - Whether on one day or on two days, as we say there (Bava Kamma 24a): Scripture made [the status of] the zav dependent upon sightings, as it is written: "And this shall be his uncleanness in his issue" (Leviticus 15:3); and [the status of] the zavah upon days, as it is written: "And if a woman have an issue of her blood many days" (Leviticus 15:25) — the minimum of [the plural] "days" is two; "many" is three.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:7:2.hebrew: בשביעי שלו - שאין בין זב רואה שתים לרואה ג' אלא קרבן, שבעל ג' מונה ז' ומביא קרבן, ובעל ב' מונה ז' ואין מביא קרבן. להכי נקט בעל שתי ראיות ושומרת יום — משום דלאו בני קרבן נינהו; דעל הנך דבני קרבן לא מצי למשחט עלייהו בשביעי, משום דלא מצו אכלי פסח בערב, דכפרת קרבן דבעו לאיתויי בשמיני מעכבת להו, כדקי"ל (יבמות דף עד:) הביא כפרתו אוכל בקדשים. אלמא מיהא, מדקתני מטמא משכב ומושב למפרע, דלא הוי טעמא דר' יוסי משום דמכאן ולהבא הוא מטמא; וטעמא — משום דמקצת היום ככולו קא פטר מלעשות פסח שני, דה"ל ככל מידי דתלי במניינא דאמרי' ביה מקצת היום ככולו, ומש"ה פטורין:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:7:2.english: On his seventh [day] - For there is no [difference] between a *zav* who sees two [sightings] and one who sees three [sightings] except for an offering: as one who experienced three [sightings] counts seven [clean days] and brings an offering, while one who experienced two counts seven and does not bring an offering. For this [reason], it specifically mentioned one who experienced two sightings and a woman who observes a day [against a day] — because they are not obligated in an offering; for regarding those who are obligated in an offering, [they] could not slaughter on their behalf on the seventh [day], because they could not eat the Paschal offering in the evening, as the atonement of the offering that they must bring on the eighth [day] prevents them [from eating sacrificial food], as we establish (Yevamot 74b): "Once he has brought his atonement [offering], he may eat of sacrificial food." In any case, it is evident from that which it teaches, "[although] they render objects for lying and sitting impure retroactively," that Rabbi Yosei's reason is not that [the discharge] renders [them] impure [only] from that point forward; and the reason he exempts [them] from observing the second *Pesaḥ* is that part of the day is like the whole of it, for it is like anything that depends on a count, regarding which we say "part of the day is like the whole of it," and for that reason they are exempt.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:8:1.hebrew: לעולם אימא לך דמכאן ולהבא הוא מטמא - ולאו טעמא דר' יוסי משום דמקצת היום ככולו, ודקאמר "למפרע מטמא" — מדרבנן הוא דקאמר, ומשום דלית בהו טומאה אלא מדרבנן, פטורין מלעשות פסח שני:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:8:1.english: Actually, I could say to you that he defiles [only] from this time onward - And Rabbi Yosei's reason is not because part of the day is like the whole of it; and that which he said, "[they] defile retroactively," it is by Rabbinic law that he said [this]. And because they have no impurity other than by Rabbinic law, they are exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ.

Rashi on Nazir 15b:8:2.hebrew: דאי ס"ד מדאורייתא - מטמאין למפרע, אפי' אמרת מקצת היום ככולו — אכתי אמאי פטורין? והא איגלאי מילתא למפרע, דבההוא שעתא דשחט ונזרק הדם — טמאה מדאורייתא הואי:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:8:2.english: As, if it enters your mind [that it is] by Torah law - [that] they impart impurity retroactively, even if you say [that] part of the day is like the whole of it, still, why are they exempt? For behold, the matter has been revealed retroactively that at that time when [the offering] was slaughtered and the blood was sprinkled, she was impure by Torah law!

Rashi on Nazir 15b:9:1.hebrew: לעולם אימא לך - דטמאין למפרע מדאורייתא, וכל היכא דתלי מילתא במניינא, כגון בשתי נזירות, שצריך למנות לזו ל' ולזו ל' — הוי מקצת היום ככולו. והכא, אע"ג דמדאורייתא מטמא למפרע, אמאי הקילו בה? היינו טעמא: דטומאה דתהום דזיבה התירו; דכיון דבההיא שעתא דנשחט אכתי הוה קיימא טיפת דם במקור של אשה ולא יצא לחוץ, אהני בה מקצת היום ככולו, דכמאן דנשחט עליה בשעת טהרה דמי. ואית דמפרשי: טומאת התהום בזיבה היינו דבשעת שחיטה וזריקה עדיין לא היתה יודעת אם תהא רואה בו ביום ואם לאו, משום הכי קרי לה טומאת תהום, דהויא טמאה למפרע בשעת שחיטה וזריקה ואיהי לא הות ידעה בההיא שעתא, ודמי לעובר ברשות הרבים וטומאת התהום תחתיו:
Rashi on Nazir 15b:9:1.english: Actually, I could say to you - That they are impure retroactively by Torah law; and wherever a matter depends on a count, such as in [the case of] two naziriteships, where one must count thirty [days] for this one and thirty [days] for that one, part of the day is like the whole of it. And here, even though by Torah law it defiles retroactively, why were they lenient regarding her? That is the reason: because they permitted [the offering in the case of] an impurity of the deep of zivah; for since at that time that [the offering] was slaughtered, the drop of blood was still present in the woman's womb and had not emerged outside, part of the day [being considered] like the whole of it was effective for her, so that it is regarded as though it was slaughtered for her at a time of purity. And some explain: Impurity of the deep regarding zivah means that at the time of slaughtering and sprinkling [the blood], she did not yet know whether she would see [a discharge] on that day or not. Because of this, [the Gemara] calls it “impurity of the deep,” for she is impure retroactively at the time of slaughtering and sprinkling, yet she did not know at that time; and it is similar to one who passes through the public domain while impurity of the deep is beneath him.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:10:1.english: "And even Rabbi Oshaya" - [This] refers back to the resolution that [impurity applying] retroactively is rabbinic.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:10:2.hebrew: אבל הרואה זוב - פי' [רש"י] בכיצד צולין (פסחים ד' פא.): לא ידעינן אהיכא קאי:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:10:2.english: "However, one who sees discharge" - [Rashi] explained in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (Pesachim 81a): We do not know what [the word "however"] refers to.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:10:3.hebrew: סותר את שלפניו כו' - ספורים שספר, וצריך למנות ז' ימים אחרים:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:10:3.english: "Negates that which preceded it, etc." - [The days] counted that he had counted, and he must count another seven days.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:10:4.hebrew: [א"ל ר"י לא נסתור אלא יומו] - יחזור ויספור יום אחד. והוינן בה במילתא דר' יוחנן: אי סתר — כולהו בעי למיסתר, דכתיב: "וספרה לה ז' ימים לטהרתה", שלא תהא טומאה מפסקת בינתים. בפרק כיצד צולין גרס: "[אי קסבר למפרע הוא מטמא — אפילו כולהו נסתור], ואי מכאן ולהבא הוא מטמא — יומו נמי לא נסתור", דהרי היא כראיה ראשונה של זיבה אחרת, ואין בה אלא טומאת ערב, ויטבול לערב ויטהר, דקי"ל: ראיה ראשונה של זב קרי בעלמא הוא:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:10:4.english: ["Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: Let it negate only its own day"] - He must go back and count one day. And we discussed the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan: If it negates, it should need to negate all of them, for it is written: “And she shall count for herself seven days for her purification” — [meaning] that impurity should not interrupt in between! In the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin, [the Gemara] has the reading: “[If he holds it renders impure retroactively, let it negate even all of them;] and if [he holds] it renders impure from now and onward, let it not negate even its own day” — for behold, it is like a first sighting of another [new] zivah, which entails only impurity until evening, and he may immerse and become pure at evening, as we hold: A first sighting of a zav is merely like [a discharge of] semen.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:11:1.hebrew: ה"ק לא יסתור ולא יומו - כלומר: אפי' יומו — לפי שכבר עלה לו מקצת היום, ושלמו לו ספורים שלו, ויצא מכלל הזיבה:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:11:1.english: This is what [the Gemara] is saying: "It does not negate, and not its day" - That is to say, even its own day [it does not negate], because part of the day has already counted for him, and his counting is complete, and he has departed from the category of zivah.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:1:1.hebrew: אבא שאול אומר אפילו לא סיפר ערב הרגל מותר לספר אחר הרגל - פליג את"ק, דסבר דרגל מבטל בכל [ענין]. ופליג באחריתי: שכשם שמצות [ג'] מבטלת גזירת ז' כך מצות ז' מבטלת גזירת ל'; ופליג את"ק דמצריך ח' — לאו משום דקסבר יום ז' עולה לו למנין שבעה ומקצתו עולה למנין ל', אע"פ שעומד באמצע אבילות:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:1:1.english: Abba Shaul says: Even if he did not cut his hair on the eve of the Festival, it is permitted to cut his hair after the Festival - [Abba Shaul] disagrees with the First Tanna, as he maintains that the Festival voids [the thirty-day restrictions] under all circumstances. And he [also] disagrees on another [matter]: that just as the observance of three [days] voids the decree of seven, so the observance of seven voids the decree of thirty; and [thus] he disagrees with the First Tanna, who requires eight [days]. [And is this] not because he holds that the seventh day counts for him toward the count of seven, and part of it counts toward the count of thirty, even though he is in the midst of mourning?

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:2:1.hebrew: אלא באבילות דרבנן - דמן התורה אינו אבל אלא יום ראשון, כדכתיב: "ואחריתה כיום מר"; אבל בנזירות דאורייתא, דדרשינן מקרא דבעינן ל' יום — לא אמרי' דמקצת יום עולה לו לכאן ולכאן:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:2:1.english: "Only with regard to rabbinic mourning" - For by Torah law, one is a mourner only on the first day, as it is written: "And the end thereof as a bitter day" (Amos 8:10); but regarding naziriteship, which is by Torah law, where we derive from Scripture that thirty days are required, we do not say that part of a day counts for both here and there.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:3:1.hebrew: ששחטו וזרקו עליה בשני - שחל בערב פסח, ושחטו עליה הפסח, ואח"כ ראתה — הרי זו אינה אוכלת בלילה בפסח, לפי [שהיא] נטמאה; ופטורה מלעשות פסח שני, דבשעת שחיטה טהורה היתה:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:3:1.english: "Where they slaughtered and sprinkled for her on the second [day]" - [That is, a case where her second day] coincided with Passover eve, and they slaughtered the Paschal offering on her behalf, and afterwards she saw [blood] — this [woman] may not eat from the Paschal offering at night, because [she] became impure; yet she is exempt from observing the second Passover, since at the time of slaughter she was pure.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:5:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא דר' יוסי (הגלילי) לאו משום מקצת היום ככולו - ומכאן ולהבא היא מטמאה (דאתמול), נמצא כי בשעת שחיטה וזריקה היתה טהורה גמורה, דמכאן ולהבא היא מטמאה ולא למפרע. וכי הדרא חזיא — מטמאינן לה מכאן ולהבא, ולמחר תעשה שימור גמור למקצת יום זה שנטמאת. אלמא דיום שני זה: מקצת יום חשבינן ליה יום טהור דליהוי שימור ליום שאתמול, הילכך שחיטה וזריקה בטהרה היה; ומקצתו חשבינן ליה יום טומאה, דליהוי יום של מחר שימור להאי מקצת יום. אבל רבנן פליגי ומטמאי למפרע, וחשבינן זה היום ככולו טמא [כיום] של אתמול. ורב דאמר כר' יוסי — ואע"ג דהכא נמי היה סברא לחשיבת יום ככולו טמא כיום שלפניו כסברא דרבנן, אפ"ה ר' יוסי מחשיבו לכאן ולכאן, והיינו כסברת רב. וזו שכתוב בספרים "ודילמא משום דקסבר" — לא גרסינן ליה, דאי לאו הכי, מה מהני שאינו מטמא למפרע:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:5:1.english: "What is the rationale of Rabbi Yosei (HaGelili)? Isn’t it because [he holds] part of the day is like the whole of it?" - And she becomes impure [only] from now and onward (for yesterday[’s discharge]); it turns out that at the time of the slaughter and sprinkling she was completely pure, for she becomes impure from now and onward, and not retroactively. And when she sees [blood] again, we render her impure from now and onward, and tomorrow she will observe a complete [day of] guarding for the part of this day that she became impure. It follows that regarding this second day: part of the day we reckon as a pure day so that it serves as guarding for yesterday’s day — consequently, the slaughter and sprinkling were [performed] in purity; and part of it we reckon as an impure day so that tomorrow’s day serves as guarding for this part of the day. However, the Rabbis disagree and render [her] impure retroactively, and we reckon this day entirely as impure, like yesterday's day. And Rav, who stated [his ruling], holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei; and even though here too there was reason to reckon the day entirely as impure like the day before it, in accordance with the reasoning of the Rabbis, even so, Rabbi Yosei reckons it for here and for there, and that is identical to Rav’s reasoning. And that which is written in the books, "And perhaps because he holds...", we do not read in the text; for if it were not so, what does it help that she does not become impure retroactively?

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:7:1.hebrew: זב בעל שתי ראיות - דאילו בעל שלשה, לא חזי למיכל [לאחר דראה שלישית] עד יום ח' שיביא קרבנותיו; וביום ח' לא מצי למינקט: "ואח"כ ראה מטמא משכב ומושב למפרע", דמיום ז' ואילך פסק מסתירה, ומשכב ומושב דמאתמול שאחר הטבילה עד הנה טהורין, ואפי' ראה היום ביום ח' — לא מטמא למפרע:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:7:1.english: A zav who experienced two sightings - For had [the baraita spoken of] one who experienced three [sightings], he would not be fit to eat [the Paschal offering] [after having seen a third sighting] until the eighth day, when he brings his offerings. And on the eighth day, [the tanna] could not formulate: "and afterward he saw [a discharge], he renders objects designed for lying and sitting impure retroactively," because from the seventh day onward, cancellation [of the clean days] has ceased, and objects designed for lying and sitting from yesterday that were [used] after the immersion until now are pure, and even if he saw [a discharge] today on the eighth day, he does not render [them] impure retroactively.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:7:2.hebrew: אע"פ שמטמאין משכב ומושב למפרע - ואפילו טבל בשביעי, משכבות דלאחר טבילה טמאין; סתר מניינו, והרי הוא כתחילתו, דכתיב: "וספרה לה שבעת ימים", והרי אין כאן ז' ימים. ומדקתני בשמירת יום למפרע טומאה, אלמא לא אמר מקצת יום ככולו, וקשיא דר' יוסי אדר' יוסי. ומשני: למפרע — מדרבנן, אבל מן התורה — טהורה:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:7:2.english: “Although they render objects designed for lying and sitting impure retroactively” - And even if he immersed on the seventh [day], objects designed for lying upon [used] after immersion are impure; [for] he has negated his count and he is as at the beginning [of his impurity], as it is written: “And she shall count for herself seven days” (Leviticus 15:28) — and behold, there are not seven days here. And since it teaches retroactive impurity regarding a woman observing a day [for a day], this implies that he does not say [that] part of the day is like the whole of it; and [this statement of] Rabbi Yosei contradicts [the other statement of] Rabbi Yosei. And [the Gemara] answers: [The impurity applies] retroactively [only] by rabbinic law, but by Torah law, she is ritually pure.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:8:1.hebrew: הכי נמי מסתברא וכו' - ודחי: אימא לך טומאת התהום דזיבה התירו. כלומר: אימא לך שמטמאין למפרע מדאורייתא, ופטורין לעשות פסח שני — דהלכה למשה מסיני דטומאה דמת הותרה לעושי פסח, והאי תנא ס"ל דאפי' טומאת התהום דזיבה הותרה לעושי הפסח:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:8:1.english: "So too, it is reasonable, etc." - And [the Gemara] rejects [this]: I could say to you [that] the impurity of the deep of zivah was permitted. That is to say: I could say to you that they render [items] impure retroactively by Torah law, and [yet] they are exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ, for [there is] a halakhah le-Moshe mi-Sinai that corpse impurity was permitted to those offering the Paschal lamb, and this tanna maintains that even the impurity of the deep of zivah was permitted to those offering the Paschal lamb.

Tosafot on Nazir 15b:9:1.hebrew: התהום - פי': דבשעת שחיטה ישב על אבן אחת, ולא נודע כלל שקבר תחתיו, עד אחר שחיטה נודע לו שניטמא בקבר התהום. וכן הכא: לא ידע אדם בשעת שחיטה אם אחרי כן תראה ותסתור להיות טמאה; וטומאת התהום [התירו] לעושי הפסח ונזיר:
Tosafot on Nazir 15b:9:1.english: The deep - Explanation: For at the time of the slaughter, he sat upon a stone and it was not known at all that a grave was beneath it, until after the slaughter it became known to him that he had become impure through a grave of the deep. And similarly here, no person knew at the time of the slaughter whether she would afterward see [a discharge] and negate [her clean days] so as to become impure; and impurity of the deep [was permitted] for those who make the Paschal offering and for a nazirite.
